name: Retro Hong Kong Kung Fu Pet Short
description: Develops a person, pet, animal reference or a one-line inspiration into a 1980s retro Hong Kong kung fu comedy short; first build the complete workflow containing the script, storyboard, key elements, shot-by-shot videos and audio layers, then hand it to the canvas workflow to execute in stages.

input_parameters.label: Background music
options: Generate Hong Kong light-comedy wuxia BGM

planning.planning_notes: Before starting, judge whether the information is sufficient by combining total_duration, character_input_method, bgm_mode, aspect_ratio, the user's text inspiration and the canvas/uploaded assets. If there is neither a usable character reference nor a text inspiration, ask the director first; at that point do not create a workflow draft or canvas nodes, and do not write the entry prompt into node content. Once the information is sufficient, first confirm the global creative Brief in conversation, locking the title, duration, aspect ratio, character source, comedy direction and audio choice; the Brief serves planning only and creates no standalone node. Then list the complete workflow in the draft at once: the four-act comedy script outline, the storyboard plan, the anthropomorphic kung fu key element image stage in which independent key element nodes are created separately for independently referenceable characters/animals, scenes and key props, all the anthropomorphic kung fu single-clip videos split by the confirmed plot and target duration, and finally the video audio layer as chosen; the videos and audio finally connect to the video compose node. Do not merge multiple subjects into one key element node; only assets that are always referenced downstream as one whole may share a node. Every shot must be an independent intent item and canvas node; creating only the first stage, or one generic video node to stand in for the complete short, is not allowed. By default each shot runs in parallel: they commonly depend on the confirmed storyboard plan and the key element nodes they actually need; only when a later shot needs the previous shot's generated video as a real continuity input should dependencies and video references between shots be established. The Runner executes only nodes that have landed on the canvas and will not automatically expand later nodes from a completed outline. After the complete workflow lands on the canvas, run the story/storyboard, key element, video and audio stages in order; the output of each stage remains a reviewable node, but the creation of these nodes must not be delayed because of that. Add the audio layer to the draft only when bgm_mode selects "Generate Hong Kong light-comedy wuxia BGM" or the director explicitly asks for it. Final composition is done by the video compose node connecting the videos and audio in storyboard order, handled by canvas tools.
planning.prompt_guide: The creative core is 1980s retro Hong Kong kung fu comedy: comedy first, with kung fu as the shell; pets/animals keep their instinctive behavior, forming an absurd contrast with the wuxia styling. The global visual is warm yellow and slightly dark, low-saturation strong light, 35mm old film grain, hard-light outlines, heavy shadows with soft highlights, slightly faded reds and yellows; smoke, dust and dim yellow indoor lighting can reinforce the old Hong Kong film texture. Common scenes include old alleys, cha chaan teng diners, old martial arts schools, rooftops, bamboo forests, temples and docks. Every video node must write out, for each core action of the current shot, the three phases of preparation, motion and completion, making the body part, direction, force and completion state explicit; it must not merely write generic requirements like "actions need three phases" or "the fight is intense"; camera movement prefers push/pull, follow shots, low angles, quick cuts to reaction shots and comedic pauses. Dialogue or narration uses a Hong Kong-flavored accent and old-microphone grain.
conduct_rules: All images and videos keep the aspect ratio confirmed in input_parameters; do not change the aspect ratio on your own.
No subtitles by default; background music is generated only when chosen before starting or explicitly requested by the director.
A pet or animal must keep both its species habits and its wuxia styling, with the humor coming from the behavioral logic contrast.
The video opening should establish conflict or contrast as soon as possible, and actions must have preparation, motion and completion states.
Drone aerial shots, obvious handheld shake and an over-smooth stabilizer/slider feel are forbidden.

rating_bands.description: The dynamic stages are clear with complete stage boundaries, and Hong Kong kung fu comedy, pet instinct contrast, old film texture and the hard audio rules all land stably in every output.
The flow is basically complete, but some stages lack stage boundaries, action arcs, Hong Kong film texture, reference binding or audio/subtitle constraints.
Stages are skipped, a fixed template is applied mechanically, subtitles/BGM are added by default, the aspect ratio is wrong, or pure wuxia is treated as the comedy core.

visual_review_items.name: Retro Hong Kong film texture
visual_review_items.description: Warm yellow and slightly dark, low-saturation strong light, 35mm grain, hard-light outlines, heavy shadows with soft highlights, slightly faded reds and yellows.

visual_review_items.name: Cute pet kung fu contrast
visual_review_items.description: Animal instinct and wuxia styling coexist, with the humor coming from behavioral logic contrast rather than simply exaggerated expressions.

visual_review_items.name: Action realism
visual_review_items.description: Every action writes out preparation, motion and completion, reflecting speed, amplitude, body parts and completion state.

text_review_items.name: Stage boundaries
text_review_items.description: Each stage has a clear output, input dependencies and next step, making it easy to review and advance the canvas workflow.

text_review_items.name: Structured output
text_review_items.description: Use Markdown tables in the same language as the user's input with complete fields, convenient for downstream nodes and director edits.

domain_constraints: Follow the aspect ratio chosen before starting.
No subtitles and no background music by default.
Ambient sound is kept by default; dialogue/narration uses a Hong Kong-flavored accent and old-microphone grain.
The first 3 seconds must establish conflict or contrast.
Pets/animals must keep both their species habits and their wuxia styling.
Drone aerial shots, obvious handheld shake and an over-smooth stabilizer/slider feel are forbidden.
